title: Semantic Support Ticket Routing
business: Customer support teams managing high volumes of incoming technical inquiries.
problem: Support agents waste time manually categorizing tickets that share the same underlying technical issue but use different phrasing, leading to delayed response times.
solution: By deploying all-MiniLM-L6-v2, the system maps incoming ticket descriptions into a 384-dimensional dense vector space. This allows the organization to perform semantic search against a knowledge base of resolved issues, identifying relevant solutions even when the user's vocabulary differs from the documentation.
steps: Install the sentence-transformers library to access the model.
Load the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 model into the application environment.
Convert existing historical ticket resolutions into vector embeddings.
Encode incoming support tickets into vectors using the same model.
Calculate the cosine similarity between the new ticket vector and the historical database to retrieve the most semantically related past solutions.
outcome: Improved agent efficiency through automated retrieval of contextually relevant historical solutions, reducing the need for manual ticket classification.
limitation: The model truncates input text longer than 256 word pieces by default, which may cause loss of critical context in very long, complex technical logs or multi-paragraph descriptions. Developers should monitor input length and implement chunking strategies if necessary.

from sentence_transformers import SentenceTransformer
# Initialize the model
model = SentenceTransformer('sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2')
# Encode ticket text into a dense vector
embeddings = model.encode(['My screen is flickering during video calls'])
# The resulting embeddings can now be compared against a database of resolved issues
